Test: datagram with two envelopes: I (pn 0) then H (pn 0). Wire: envelope('I', 0, ping) + envelope('H', 0, ping).

cd /workspace/dev && python3 - <<'EOF'
from t import *

# Test 1: coalesced I + H in one datagram
wire = envelope('I', 0, b'\x01') + envelope('H', 0, b'\x01')
tr = trace([datagram(wire)])
res = run([tr])['traces'][0]
print("T1 packets:", [(p['packet'],p['offset'],p['level'],p['pn'],p['status'],p['sha256'][:8] if p['sha256'] else None) for p in res['packets']])
print("T1 datagrams:", [(d['packets'],d['accepted'],d['bytes'],d['sha256'][:8]) for d in res['datagrams']])
print("T1 received:", res['received'], "closed:", res['closed'])
print("len wire", len(wire), wire.hex())

# expected canonical envelope for I pn0 ping: c0 00000001 01aa 01bb 00 02 00 01
print("expected env bytes:", bytes.fromhex('c00000000101aa01bb00020001').hex())
# H canonical: e0 00000001 01aa 01bb 02 00 01
print("expected H bytes:", bytes.fromhex('e00000000101aa01bb020001').hex())
import hashlib
e1 = bytes.fromhex('c00000000101aa01bb00020001')
e2 = bytes.fromhex('e00000000101aa01bb020001')
print("e1 hash", hashlib.sha256(e1).hexdigest())
print("e2 hash", hashlib.sha256(e2).hexdigest())
print("combo hash", hashlib.sha256(e1+e2).hexdigest())

# Test 2: BAD_HEADER abandons datagram; later datagram still processed
bad = bytes([0xc4]) + b'\x00' * 20   # reserved bits set -> BAD_HEADER
tr2 = trace([datagram(bad), datagram(envelope('I',0,b'\x01'))])
res2 = run([tr2])['traces'][0]
print("T2 packets:", [(p['event'],p['packet'],p['offset'],p['level'],p['pn'],p['status']) for p in res2['packets']])
print("T2 datagrams:", [(d['event'],d['packets'],d['accepted'],d['bytes']) for d in res2['datagrams']])

# Test 3: duplicate detection
tr3 = trace([datagram(envelope('I',0,b'\x01')), datagram(envelope('I',0,b'\x01'))])
res3 = run([tr3])['traces'][0]
print("T3 packets:", [(p['pn'],p['status']) for p in res3['packets']])
print("T3 received:", res3['received'])
EOF
